note: Reads the entire attacker-controlled input file into a GBytes buffer; this is the entry point for all subsequent parsing.
Parses the 25-byte uSWID header (magic, hdrver, hdrsz, payloadsz, flags, compression) from the input buffer; attacker controls all header fields.
Extracts the attacker-controlled 32-bit payload size from the header; this value is used to slice the compressed payload region.
Extracts the attacker-controlled compression type byte (0=none, 1=zlib, 2=lzma) from the header; determines which decompression path is taken.

code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
note: Reads the payload bytes from the input stream using the attacker-controlled payloadsz; the payload is the compressed coSWID CBOR document.
Decompresses the payload (zlib or lzma) producing the raw coSWID CBOR bytes that are passed to the coSWID parser.
Parses the decompressed CBOR document using libcbor; the attacker controls the entire CBOR structure including map keys and values.
Gets the array of key-value pairs from the top-level CBOR map; attacker controls the number of pairs and their types.
Reads the tag ID from each map key using cbor_get_uint8; if the key is not a uint type, libcbor reads the item's data field as an integer, which can be a pointer to attacker-influenced heap data.

code: if (tag_id == FU_COSWID_TAG_ENTITY) { fu_coswid_firmware_parse_one_or_many(self, pairs[i].value, fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity, NULL, error); }
note: When the tag ID is FU_COSWID_TAG_ENTITY (3), the value is dispatched to fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity; the value can be a single map or an array of maps.
Gets the key-value pairs from the entity map; attacker controls the entity map contents including the ROLE tag.
Reads the tag ID from each entity map key; attacker controls these keys.

code: if (tag_id == FU_COSWID_TAG_ROLE) { if (cbor_isa_uint(pairs[i].value)) { FuCoswidEntityRole role = cbor_get_uint8(pairs[i].value); entity->roles[entity_role_cnt++] = role; } }
note: When the ROLE tag (33) is encountered and the value is a uint, the role is written to entity->roles[entity_role_cnt++] WITHOUT a bounds check on entity_role_cnt; the roles array has only 6 elements (G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles) == 6).

With 6 or more uint ROLE values in the entity map, entity_role_cnt exceeds 5 and the write goes past the 6-element roles array, causing a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE past the FuCoswidFirmwareEntity allocation.

code: for (guint j = 0; j < cbor_array_size(pairs[i].value); j++) { g_autoptr(cbor_item_t) value = cbor_array_get(pairs[i].value, j); FuCoswidEntityRole role = cbor_get_uint8(value); }
note: If pairs[i].value is an array, each element is read with cbor_get_uint8 without type checking; if an element is not a uint, libcbor reads item->data as an integer, which for non-uint types is a pointer into heap memory, leading to a heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 when the pointer value is dereferenced or interpreted as a 4-byte integer.
The unchecked write continues past the 6-element roles array, corrupting adjacent heap memory and triggering the ASAN heap-buffer-overflow report.
